title: Measures to Help Singaporeans Cope with Rising Inflation and Impact of Government's Fiscal Support for Businesses and Households on Inflation
what_it_is: Measures to Help Singaporeans Cope with Rising Inflation and Impact of Government's Fiscal Support for Businesses and Households on Inflation

sections.label: Inflation, GST and fiscal support
sections.summary: Questions ask whether fiscal resources can help Singaporeans with costs, whether the GST increase remains for fiscal sustainability, and how to mitigate its impact.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Finance in light of inflation and rising costs (a) whether there are available fiscal resources in the upcoming Budget to further assist Singaporeans to cope with increased costs; (b) whether the proposed GST increase remains part of our strategy for fiscal sustainability; and (c) if so, what can be done to mitigate the impact of GST increase on Singaporeans, especially the lower income households and retirees.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Finance (a) whether the economic policy involving billions of fiscal support to businesses and households is contributing to higher inflation; and (b) how will the market adjust when the support schemes taper off.

sections.label: November 2021 inflation components
sections.summary: The 3.8% November 2021 inflation rate is largely accounted for by accommodation, mainly imputed rentals, and private transport costs.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: First, while the inflation rate of 3.8% reported for November 2021 is high, a significant part of that 3.8% is accounted for by accommodation, mainly imputed rentals and private transport costs.

sections.label: MAS Core Inflation November 2021
sections.summary: MAS Core Inflation was 1.6% year-on-year in November 2021.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: MAS Core Inflation was at 1.6% year-on-year in November 2021.

sections.label: U-Save rebates and CDC Vouchers
sections.summary: HDB 1- to 2-room households received $595 in U-Save rebates in FY2021, and every Singaporean household received $100 in CDC Vouchers in December 2021.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: HDB 1- to 2-room households received $595 in U-Save rebates in FY2021, equivalent to about 4.5 to six months of their utility bills on average, even after the increase in the electricity tariff this month.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: To help households with daily expenses, especially food, the Government has given $100 in Community Development Council (CDC) Vouchers to every Singaporean household in December 2021.

sections.label: Assurance Package GST mitigation
sections.summary: The Assurance Package, with $6 billion set aside, mitigates the GST increase, delaying its impact at least five years and about 10 years for lower-income households.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: Even as we keep our finances on a sound and stable footing, we will ensure that our overall system of taxes and transfers remains a fair and progressive one.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: We will also significantly mitigate the impact of the GST rate increase on Singaporeans through the Assurance Package.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: We have already set aside $6 billion for this Package to provide direct cash and other support to Singaporeans.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: Such support will effectively delay the impact of the GST rate increase by at least five years for the majority of Singaporean households.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: Lower-income households will receive more support under the Assurance Package and for this group, the impact of the GST rate increase will be pushed back by about 10 years.

sections.label: Planned GST increase announcement
sections.summary: Budget 2018 announced a planned GST increase of two percentage points from 7% to 9%, sometime from 2021 to 2025.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: For the first one, we had announced in Budget 2018 that we plan to raise the GST by two percentage points from 7% to 9%.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: And we said then that it would be some time from 2021 to 2025.

sections.label: 2022 GDP growth forecast
sections.summary: The economy is recovering steadily and, barring fresh disruptions, GDP is expected to grow by 3% to 5% in 2022.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: The economy is recovering steadily and barring fresh disruptions, it should grow in step with global economic recovery, and we expect GDP to grow by 3% to 5% in 2022.

sections.label: Delayed impact on Singaporeans
sections.summary: For most Singaporeans the impact will be delayed effectively by five years, and for lower income earners by 10 years.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: For the majority of Singaporeans, we will delay the impact on them effectively by five years and for the lower income, the impact on them will be delayed effectively for 10 years.

sections.label: Global supply bottlenecks abating
sections.summary: There are some signs global supply bottlenecks are abating, with input price pressure easing and delivery delays shortening.

sentences.speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
sentences.text: In response to his first supplementary question, there are some signs that the global supply bottlenecks are abating, with pressure on input prices easing and we are observing that the delivery delays are shortening.

sections.label: Support for SMEs' cashflow
sections.summary: MTI, ESG and EDB are committed to supporting SMEs and local companies, with ESG working with financial institutions through the Enterprise Financing Scheme.

sentences.speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
sentences.text: To this end, MTI, ESG and EDB stand committed to support our SMEs and local companies.

sentences.speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
sentences.text: If they are facing cashflow issues arising from supply chain challenges, ESG will continue to work with participating financial institutions to support them through the Enterprise Financing Scheme.

sections.label: Conducive business environment assurance
sections.summary: The Government is committed to a conducive and competitive business environment for companies and a wide range of choices for consumers.

sentences.speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
sentences.text: That certainly helped to shape the necessary behaviour by retailers and organisations.

sentences.speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
sentences.text: So, I want to assure the Member that the Government is committed to ensuring that Singapore has a conducive and competitive business environment for companies to thrive and at the same time, a wide range of choices for our consumers.

sections.label: Temporary Bridging Loan support
sections.summary: The Temporary Bridging Loan provides up to S$3 million in working capital; from April to December 2021 over 6,000 enterprises benefited, catalysing S$1.8 billion in loans.

sentences.speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
sentences.text: Businesses can make use of the Temporary Bridging Loan (TBL) which provides additional working capital support of up to S$3 million for enterprises.

sentences.speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
sentences.text: From April to December 2021, more than 6,000 enterprises have benefited from the TBL.

sentences.speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
sentences.text: This amounted to S$1.8 billion worth of loans being catalysed.

sections.label: JSS support disbursed
sections.summary: More than S$28 billion of JSS support has been disbursed since the scheme was introduced in February 2020.

sentences.speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
sentences.text: To date, more than S$28 billion of JSS support has been disbursed since the scheme was introduced in February 2020.

sections.label: Income, education, healthcare, housing schemes
sections.summary: Structural schemes uplift incomes, and subsidies are provided for education, healthcare and housing.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: The second thing we do is we have structural schemes to uplift and supplement their incomes.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: This includes the Progressive Wage Model, as well as the Workfare Income Supplement Scheme.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: Every Singaporean child could receive about $180,000 in education subsidies by the time he or she turns 16, including preschool subsidies, with more for those who come from less well-off backgrounds.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: And for healthcare, we have many schemes, such as CHAS, the Pioneer Generation Package and the Merdeka Generation Package.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: We also provide housing subsidies to keep HDB flats affordable, so eligible first-timer households buying a resale flat could enjoy up to about $160,000 in housing grants and around 80% of new HDB flat buyers have little or no cash outlay on their mortgage payments.

sections.label: Inflation rates month-on-month
sections.summary: The November 2021 all items inflation rate was 3.8% year-on-year, 6.2% month-on-month and 7% on a three-month average.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Both of them cited how the latest 2021 November all items inflation rate was 3.8% and that is true when measured on a year-on-year basis.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: But if you look at all items analysed from the month-on-month basis, it is actually 6.2% and even if we use the average from the past three months, it is even higher at 7%.

sections.label: CPI inflation by income group
sections.summary: In Q3 2021, CPI all items inflation was 1.9% for the lowest 20%, 2.2% for the middle 60% and 3.0% for the highest 20%.

sentences.speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
sentences.text: If I could use this opportunity to share with the House, in Q3 2021, the CPI all items inflation came in at 1.9% year-on-year for the lowest 20%; and 2.2% year-on-year for the middle 60%; and 3.0% year-on-year for the highest 20% income group.

sections.label: Pandemic and real wage growth
sections.summary: The House is still in the thick of the COVID-19 pandemic, and real wage growth for the lower income was 4.6% in 2021.

sentences.speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
sentences.text: In fact, I think Minister Lawrence and Minister Gan will say that we are still in the thick of the COVID-19 pandemic.

sentences.speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
sentences.text: And for the lower income, the real wage growth was, I cited, 4.6% for the year 2021.

sections.label: MAS core inflation outlook
sections.summary: MAS core inflation is expected to increase in the first half of 2022 before easing later in the year.

sentences.speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
sentences.text: And I talked about the CPI all items inflation and then I cited the MAS core inflation.

sentences.speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
sentences.text: So, let me repeat: MAS core inflation is expected to increase in the first half of 2022, before easing in the later part of the year.

sections.label: MAS Core Inflation forecast
sections.summary: MAS Core Inflation could average within the upper half of the official forecast range of 1% to 2% for the full year.

sentences.speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
sentences.text: For the full year MAS Core Inflation, it could average within the upper half of the official forecast range of 1% to 2%.

sections.label: Government shares inflation concerns
sections.summary: The Government understands and shares Singaporeans' concerns about rising prices and inflation, and no departure was cited from Minister Chan's sharing.

sentences.speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
sentences.text: And I do not think there has been a departure between what I have cited and what Minister Chan had shared.

sentences.speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
sentences.text: I want to thank him and I want to also use this platform to reiterate again, the Government understands and shares Singaporeans' concerns about rising prices and inflation.

sections.label: Agencies managing costs and inflation
sections.summary: MTI and economic agencies work to keep a lid on business cost increases by managing domestic supply side constraints, and will monitor prices and adjust policies if needed.

sentences.speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
sentences.text: I want to use this platform to reiterate again that MTI and all our economic agencies are working very hard, in particular, in the last two years, to keep a lid on business cost increases and we do so by carefully managing our domestic supply side constraints.

sentences.speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
sentences.text: And in terms of prices, coming back to it, we will continue to monitor prices and inflation very closely and we are prepared to adjust policies where necessary.

sentences.speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
sentences.text: We understand the concerns of businesses and Singaporeans and we will do whatever we can to mitigate the cost pressures that are being felt and the effects of inflation.
